segments.en: Hello, English learners.
segments.zh: 各位英语学习者，大家好。

segments.en: Welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: And my name is Katherine.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳。

segments.en: And today we're talking about something very serious.
segments.zh: 今天我们谈论的是非常严肃的事情。

segments.en: Very serious.
segments.zh: 很严重。

segments.en: Today we're talking about capital punishment.
segments.zh: 今天我们说的是死刑。

segments.en: So if you've never heard that phrase before, you might have heard another name for this topic.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您以前从未听过该短语，您可能听说过有关此主题的另一个名称。

segments.en: It's called the death penalty.
segments.zh: 这被称为死刑。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So if you commit a crime and basically the judge says that you will have to be put to death for that crime.
segments.zh: 因此，如果您犯罪，基本上法官说您将不得不因该罪行而被处死。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So many countries no longer have this.
segments.zh: 这么多国家已经没有这个了。

segments.en: This law, the United States, you can see it in some places, some states, but not in others.
segments.zh: 这项法律，美国，你可以在某些地方、一些州看到它，但在其他地方却看不到它。

segments.en: So what we're talking about today is the debate between to have the death penalty and to not have it.
segments.zh: 所以我们今天谈论的是死刑和没有死刑之间的争论。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we're going to actually have a little debate in the end of if we agree that we should have the death penalty or not.
segments.zh: 因此，如果我们同意是否应该判处死刑，我们实际上会在结束时进行一些辩论。

segments.en: But before that, why don't we listen to this dialogue for the first time?
segments.zh: 但在此之前，我们为什么不第一次听这个对话呢？

segments.en: That's all for today's class.
segments.zh: 这就是今天的课堂的全部内容。

segments.en: We will continue our lecture on crime and punishment tomorrow.
segments.zh: 明天我们将继续我们关于犯罪和惩罚的讲座。

segments.en: Do you think we should be tougher on crime?
segments.zh: 你认为我们应该对犯罪更严厉吗？

segments.en: Well, it depends on what you mean.
segments.zh: 嗯，这取决于你的意思。

segments.en: For example, we could bring back the death penalty for murder, give longer prison sentences for lesser offenses and lock up juvenile offenders.
segments.zh: 比如，恢复对谋杀罪的死刑，加重较轻罪行的刑期，并把少年犯关进监狱。

segments.en: Those sound like really draconian measures.
segments.zh: 这些措施听起来太严苛了。

segments.en: Firstly, what do you do about miscarriages of justice if you've already put innocent people to death?
segments.zh: 首先，如果你已经把无辜的人处死了，你会怎么处理误判？

segments.en: You'd only use capital punishment if you were absolutely sure that you convicted the right person.
segments.zh: 只有当你绝对确定自己定罪了正确的人时，你才会使用死刑。

segments.en: But there have been many cases of wrongful conviction where people have been imprisoned for many years.
segments.zh: 但有很多冤案，无辜者因此被关了很多年。

segments.en: The authorities were sure at the time, but later it was shown that the evidence was unreliable.
segments.zh: 当局当时确信，但后来证明证据不可靠。

segments.en: In some cases, it had been fabricated by the police.
segments.zh: 在某些情况下，它是由警察捏造的。

segments.en: Well, no system of justice can be perfect, but surely there's a good case for longer prison sentences to deter serious crime.
segments.zh: 好吧，没有一个司法系统是完美的，但肯定有一个很好的理由可以判处更长的监禁来阻止严重的犯罪。

segments.en: I doubt whether they could act as an effective deterrent while the detection rate is so low.
segments.zh: 破案率这么低，我怀疑加重刑罚能否有效震慑犯罪。

segments.en: The best way to prevent crime is to convince people who commit it that they're going to be caught.
segments.zh: 防止犯罪的最好方法是说服犯罪的人他们会被抓获。

segments.en: It doesn't make sense to divert all your resources into the prison system.
segments.zh: 将所有资源转移到监狱系统中是没有意义的。

segments.en: But if you detect more crimes, you'll still need prisons.
segments.zh: 但如果你发现更多的犯罪，你仍然需要监狱。

segments.en: In my reckoning, if we could lock up more juvenile criminals, they'd learn that they can't get away with it.
segments.zh: 我觉得，如果把更多少年犯关进监狱，他们就会知道犯了法逃不过惩罚。

segments.en: Soft sentences will merely encourage them to do it again.
segments.zh: 量刑太轻只会鼓励他们再犯。

segments.en: Yes, but remember that prisons are often schools for criminals.
segments.zh: 是的，但请记住，监狱通常是犯罪分子的学校。

segments.en: To remove crime from society, you really have to tackle its causes.
segments.zh: 要从社会中消除犯罪，你真的必须解决它的原因。

segments.en: Well, if I were president, I would impose tougher laws and punishment.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果我是总统，我会施加更严格的法律和惩罚。

segments.en: I would have a peaceful society based on fear of punishment, not consciousness of doing the right thing.
segments.zh: 我将拥有一个基于对惩罚的恐惧的和平社会，而不是做正确的事的意识。

segments.en: You sound like a dictator.
segments.zh: 你听起来像个独裁者。

segments.en: Well, if it works, why not?
segments.zh: 好吧，如果它有效，为什么不呢？

segments.en: All right, so Marco, there's a lot of really great legal terms here, legal and crime terms.
segments.zh: 好吧，马可，这里有很多非常棒的法律术语，法律和犯罪条款。

segments.en: And so let's look at a few of these in today's Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以让我们看看今天的语言外卖中的一些。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: All right, so let's take a look at the first one.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们来看看第一个。

segments.en: They mentioned juvenile offenders.
segments.zh: 他们提到了少年犯。

segments.en: All right, so let's look at these two words because, well, offender can be pretty general.
segments.zh: 好吧，让我们看看这两个词，因为，好吧，罪犯可以很笼统。

segments.en: It's someone who commits a crime.
segments.zh: 这是犯罪的人。

segments.en: So an offender.
segments.zh: 所以罪犯。

segments.en: But we're talking about a special kind of offender.
segments.zh: 但我们谈论的是一种特殊的罪犯。

segments.en: Here we're talking about juvenile offenders.
segments.zh: 在这里，我们谈论的是少年犯。

segments.en: So they're young offenders.
segments.zh: 所以他们是年轻的罪犯。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: In America, legally, you're a juvenile offender if you're under the age of 18.
segments.zh: 在美国，在法律上，如果您未满 18 岁，您就是一名少年犯。

segments.en: Okay, so if you commit a crime while you are a juvenile, you get judged differently, right?
segments.zh: 好吧，所以如果你在青少年时期犯罪，你会受到不同的判断，对吧？

segments.en: You don't get the same treatment as an adult.
segments.zh: 你没有得到与成年人相同的待遇。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Usually, the punishments are not as harsh because people like to think that younger people, younger children or teenagers, they don't really understand the law.
segments.zh: 通常，惩罚没有那么严厉，因为人们喜欢认为年轻人、年幼的孩子或青少年，他们并不真正了解法律。

segments.en: They don't really understand crime or good and bad.
segments.zh: 他们并不真正了解犯罪或好坏。

segments.en: So it should be easier on them.
segments.zh: 所以对他们来说应该更容易。

segments.en: All right, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So we have juvenile offenders and we also have wrongful conviction.
segments.zh: 所以我们有少年犯，我们也有错误的定罪。

segments.en: All right, this is an uh-oh moment for a judge because a wrongful conviction, well, conviction first of all is a decision.
segments.zh: 好吧，这对法官来说是一个呃-哦时刻，因为错误的定罪，嗯，首先是一个决定。

segments.en: So this is a court's decision on whether or not a person is guilty.
segments.zh: 因此，这是法院对一个人是否有罪的决定。

segments.en: So you convicted the person.
segments.zh: 所以你把这个人定罪了。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Marco was convicted guilty of stealing my computer.
segments.zh: 马可因窃取我的电脑而被判有罪。

segments.en: I was too.
segments.zh: 我也是。

segments.en: That happened.
segments.zh: 那发生了。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: But it's a wrongful conviction if Marco didn't really steal a computer but we decided that he did.
segments.zh: 但如果马可没有真正窃取电脑，这是一种错误的信念，但我们决定他这样做了。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So it was a wrong decision.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个错误的决定。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: It was a bad decision in the sense that it's actually not what happened in reality.
segments.zh: 这是一个糟糕的决定，因为它实际上不是现实中发生的事情。

segments.en: A wrongful conviction.
segments.zh: 错误的信念。

segments.en: Very good.
segments.zh: 很好。

segments.en: And actually related to a wrongful conviction, many times it happens because evidence is fabricated by the police.
segments.zh: 实际上与不法定罪有关，很多时候它的发生是因为证据是由警察捏造的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So this is a big no-no.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个很大的禁忌。

segments.en: This is something that really shouldn't happen and it's against the law in many countries.
segments.zh: 这是真正不应该发生的事情，而且在许多国家都是违法的。

segments.en: So fabrication or to fabricate is to fake, to make something up.
segments.zh: 所以制造或制造就是假装，编造一些东西。

segments.en: And so evidence that's fabricated is evidence that the police or other people create to try and make someone look guilty but it's not actually evidence.
segments.zh: 因此，被捏造的证据证明了警察或其他人为试图让某人看起来有罪而创造的证据，但这实际上不是证据。

segments.en: It's not really.
segments.zh: 这不是真的。

segments.en: That's not true.
segments.zh: 那不是真的。

segments.en: It's not true.
segments.zh: 这不是真的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And now moving on, they were talking about a deterrent for crime.
segments.zh: 现在继续前进，他们谈论的是对犯罪的威慑。

segments.en: Okay, so to deter is a verb.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以要阻止是动词。

segments.en: To deter means to try and get someone to not do something.
segments.zh: 阻止意味着尝试让某人不做某事。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So I'm going to try and deter my staff from taking early lunch breaks.
segments.zh: 所以我要试着阻止我的员工提早午休。

segments.en: So I'm going to punish someone as a deterrent.
segments.zh: 所以我要惩罚某人作为威慑。

segments.en: As a deterrent.
segments.zh: 作为威慑。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So you have the verb deter and you have the noun a deterrent.
segments.zh: 所以你有动词 deter，你有名词 deterrent。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And so oftentimes very strict laws are meant to be deterrents.
segments.zh: 因此，非常严格的法律通常意味着威慑。

segments.en: They're meant to keep people from doing bad things, from breaking the law.
segments.zh: 它们旨在防止人们做坏事，不触犯法律。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So for example, capital punishment is one of those deterrents.
segments.zh: 因此，例如，死刑是这些威慑之一。

segments.en: If you kill somebody, then if you get caught, you are also going to be killed.
segments.zh: 如果你杀了一个人，那么如果你被抓住了，你也会被杀。

segments.en: So that means I'm never going to kill anyone because I don't want the law to decide that I'm going to get killed.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着我永远不会杀死任何人，因为我不希望法律决定我会被杀。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And our last word for today, they were talking about imposing tougher laws.
segments.zh: 而我们今天的最后一句话，他们谈论的是实施更严格的法律。

segments.en: I would impose tougher laws.
segments.zh: 我会施加更严格的法律。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So to impose is a verb that means to put in place or to set up or enact.
segments.zh: 所以强加是一个动词，意思是放置或设置或制定。

segments.en: And so...
segments.zh: 所以……

segments.en: You don't really impose, right?
segments.zh: 你真的不强加，对吧？

segments.en: You don't really agree to do it.
segments.zh: 你真的不同意这样做。

segments.en: Like the dictator imposes his will.
segments.zh: 就像独裁者强加他的意志。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So he makes everyone do what he wants.
segments.zh: 所以他让每个人都做他想做的事。

segments.en: But we can impose measures that do something.
segments.zh: 但我们可以强加一些做某事的措施。

segments.en: It's kind of like forcibly making people follow some kind of rule or follow a person.
segments.zh: 这有点像强行让人们遵守某种规则或遵循一个人。

segments.en: Now sometimes you would see that you have a company or you have people at your house and they're like, well, you know, stay over for dinner.
segments.zh: 现在有时你会看到你有一家公司，或者你家里有人，他们就像，嗯，你知道，留下来吃晚饭。

segments.en: And they're like, oh, I wouldn't want to impose.
segments.zh: 他们就像，哦，我不想强加。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Well, I wouldn't want to bother you or I wouldn't want to create more work for you because, you know, when you're making food, you have all these people, they don't want to impose on you.
segments.zh: 好吧，我不想打扰你，或者我不想为你创造更多的作品，因为，你知道，当你在做食物时，你有所有这些人，他们不想强加给你。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's another way of using this, impose on somebody.
segments.zh: 所以这是使用它的另一种方式，强加给某人。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So after all of these words that we've taken a look at, why don't we start now with Fluency Builder?
segments.zh: 所以在我们看过所有这些词之后，我们为什么不现在从 Fluency Builder 开始呢？

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So as you know, Fluency Builder is a place where we get to talk about some phrases and words that allow you to be more fluent in English.
segments.zh: 如您所知，Fluency Builder 是我们可以谈论一些让您更流利的英语的短语和单词的地方。

segments.en: So these are sometimes idioms or sometimes phrases, words that go together commonly.
segments.zh: 所以这些有时是成语，有时是短语，通常是一起出现的单词。

segments.en: And the first one is no exception.
segments.zh: 第一个也不例外。

segments.en: It's a miscarriage.
segments.zh: 这是流产。

segments.en: So miscarriage of justice.
segments.zh: 所以误判。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: A miscarriage of justice.
segments.zh: 正义的流产。

segments.en: Now we have different words here.
segments.zh: 现在我们在这里有不同的词。

segments.en: The first one, miscarriage, it's usually related to a medical term.
segments.zh: 第一个，流产，它通常与医学术语有关。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: It's a pregnancy.
segments.zh: 这是怀孕。

segments.en: Well, it's a pregnancy that has a sad result.
segments.zh: 好吧，这是一次怀孕，结果很悲惨。

segments.en: It's a pregnancy where the woman's baby dies or the woman loses the baby.
segments.zh: 这是妇女的婴儿死亡或妇女失去婴儿的怀孕。

segments.en: And a miscarriage of justice is a metaphor.
segments.zh: 误判是一个隐喻。

segments.en: It's a way to say that justice was not carried out.
segments.zh: 这是一种说正义没有得到伸张的方式。

segments.en: It means that, for example, with those wrongful convictions, the law failed.
segments.zh: 这意味着，例如，在那些不正当的信念中，法律失败了。

segments.en: To accomplish its objective.
segments.zh: 实现其目标。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: To accomplish its objective and to be fair.
segments.zh: 实现其目标和公平。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a miscarriage of justice.
segments.zh: 所以正义的流产。

segments.en: Interesting.
segments.zh: 有意思。

segments.en: And moving on to our next phrase, they were talking and discussing this whole death penalty situation and she mentioned, in my reckoning.
segments.zh: 继续我们的下一句话，他们在我的估计中提到和讨论了整个死刑情况，她提到。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is a great way to share your opinion or your idea with someone.
segments.zh: 因此，这是与某人分享您的意见或想法的好方法。

segments.en: You're saying pretty much, in my opinion, in my, according to me or, you know, the way I'm thinking is this.
segments.zh: 在我看来，在我看来，或者，你知道，我的想法几乎是这样的。

segments.en: So I can also say, I reckon, right?
segments.zh: 所以我也可以说，我认为，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: I reckon it's going to rain later.
segments.zh: 我估计以后会下雨的。

segments.en: I think it's going to rain.
segments.zh: 我想会下雨。

segments.en: So in my reckoning, in my opinion.
segments.zh: 所以在我的计算中，在我看来。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: I reckon.
segments.zh: 我估计。

segments.en: And to finish off Fluency Builder, they said that the person or the criminal couldn't get away with it.
segments.zh: 为了完成 Fluency Builder，他们说这个人或罪犯无法侥幸逃脱。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So this is another one of those phrases that each word maybe means something different.
segments.zh: 所以这是另一个短语中的另一个，每个单词可能意味着不同的东西。

segments.en: You can get somewhere.
segments.zh: 你可以到某个地方。

segments.en: But put together, to get away with something means to do something bad or illegal or that's not okay without getting caught.
segments.zh: 但放在一起，逃避一些事情意味着做一些不好的或非法的事情，或者在不被抓住的情况下是不行的。

segments.en: Or being punished.
segments.zh: 或受到惩罚。

segments.en: Or being punished.
segments.zh: 或受到惩罚。

segments.en: So you can say, get away with murder.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说，逃避谋杀。

segments.en: He got away with murder.
segments.zh: 他逃脱了谋杀。

segments.en: You know, he did something that was really, really bad but no one caught him.
segments.zh: 你知道，他做了一些非常非常糟糕的事情，但没有人抓住他。

segments.en: And also it means the criminal got away so they couldn't catch him.
segments.zh: 这也意味着罪犯逃走了，所以他们无法抓住他。

segments.en: Or I could always say to my brother, he would always lie to my parents and get away with it.
segments.zh: 或者我总是可以对我的兄弟说，他总是对我的父母撒谎并侥幸逃脱。

segments.en: So he never got caught.
segments.zh: 所以他从来没有被抓住。

segments.en: He never got punished.
segments.zh: 他从未受到惩罚。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So he got away with his lie or got away, got his way.
segments.zh: 所以他逃脱了他的谎言或逃脱了，得到了他的方式。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So I think this is an interesting phrase.
segments.zh: 所以我认为这是一个有趣的短语。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to a couple of more examples.
segments.zh: 我们为什么不听更多的例子。

segments.en: Example one.
segments.zh: 例句一。

segments.en: Do you think we could get away with using the cheaper product?
segments.zh: 您认为我们可以使用更便宜的产品吗？

segments.en: Example two.
segments.zh: 例句二。

segments.en: Thieves got away with two Picassos which were never found.
segments.zh: 小偷逃脱了两个从未被发现的毕加索。

segments.en: Example three.
segments.zh: 例句三。

segments.en: He almost got away with murder.
segments.zh: 他几乎逃脱了谋杀。

segments.en: Unfortunately for him, the police discovered his secret.
segments.zh: 对他来说不幸的是，警察发现了他的秘密。

segments.en: So we've taken a look at a lot of great phrases.
segments.zh: 所以我们看了很多很棒的短语。

segments.en: Why don't we listen to our dialogue for the last time and then we'll come back.
segments.zh: 为什么我们不听我们最后一次的对话，然后我们会回来。

segments.en: That's all for today's class.
segments.zh: 这就是今天的课堂的全部内容。

segments.en: We will continue our lecture on crime and punishment tomorrow.
segments.zh: 明天我们将继续我们关于犯罪和惩罚的讲座。

segments.en: Do you think we should be tougher on crime?
segments.zh: 你认为我们应该对犯罪更严厉吗？

segments.en: Well it depends on what you mean.
segments.zh: 好吧，这取决于你的意思。

segments.en: For example, we could bring back the death penalty for murder, give longer prison sentences for lesser offenses, and lock up juvenile offenders.
segments.zh: 例如，我们可以将谋杀罪判处死刑，对轻罪判处更长的监禁，并锁定少年犯。

segments.en: Those sound like really draconian measures.
segments.zh: 这些听起来像是真正的严厉措施。

segments.en: Firstly, what do you do about miscarriages of justice if you've already put innocent people to death?
segments.zh: 首先，如果你已经把无辜的人处死了，你会怎么处理误判？

segments.en: You'd only use capital punishment if you were absolutely sure that you convicted the right person.
segments.zh: 只有当你绝对确定自己定罪了正确的人时，你才会使用死刑。

segments.en: But there have been many cases of wrongful conviction where people have been imprisoned for many years.
segments.zh: 但有很多冤案，无辜者因此被关了很多年。

segments.en: The authorities were sure at the time, but later it was shown that the evidence was unreliable.
segments.zh: 当局当时确信，但后来证明证据不可靠。

segments.en: In some cases, it had been fabricated by the police.
segments.zh: 在某些情况下，它是由警察捏造的。

segments.en: Well, no system of justice can be perfect, but surely there's a good case for longer prison sentences to deter serious crime.
segments.zh: 好吧，没有一个司法系统是完美的，但肯定有一个很好的理由可以判处更长的监禁来阻止严重的犯罪。

segments.en: I doubt whether they could act as an effective deterrent while the detection rate is so low.
segments.zh: 破案率这么低，我怀疑加重刑罚能否有效震慑犯罪。

segments.en: The best way to prevent crime is to convince people who commit it that they're going to be caught.
segments.zh: 防止犯罪的最好方法是说服犯罪的人他们会被抓获。

segments.en: It doesn't make sense to divert all your resources into the prison system.
segments.zh: 将所有资源转移到监狱系统中是没有意义的。

segments.en: But if you detect more crimes, you'll still need prisons.
segments.zh: 但如果你发现更多的犯罪，你仍然需要监狱。

segments.en: In my reckoning, if we could lock up more juvenile criminals, they'd learn that they can't get away with it.
segments.zh: 我觉得，如果把更多少年犯关进监狱，他们就会知道犯了法逃不过惩罚。

segments.en: Soft sentences will merely encourage them to do it again.
segments.zh: 量刑太轻只会鼓励他们再犯。

segments.en: Yes, but remember that prisons are often schools for criminals.
segments.zh: 是的，但请记住，监狱通常是犯罪分子的学校。

segments.en: To remove crime from society, you really have to tackle its causes.
segments.zh: 要从社会中消除犯罪，你真的必须解决它的原因。

segments.en: Well, if I were president, I would impose tougher laws and punishment.
segments.zh: 好吧，如果我是总统，我会施加更严格的法律和惩罚。

segments.en: I would have a peaceful society based on fear of punishment, not consciousness of doing the right thing.
segments.zh: 我将拥有一个基于对惩罚的恐惧的和平社会，而不是做正确的事的意识。

segments.en: You sound like a dictator.
segments.zh: 你听起来像个独裁者。

segments.en: Well, if it works, why not?
segments.zh: 好吧，如果它有效，为什么不呢？

segments.en: All right, so now the big question, Catherine, do you agree with the death penalty?
segments.zh: 好吧，那么现在最大的问题是，凯瑟琳，你同意死刑吗？

segments.en: Oh, this is a big one, and I don't think we have enough time to go into it in much detail here, but I definitely think that is extreme, right?
segments.zh: 哦，这是一个很大的问题，我认为我们没有足够的时间在这里详细介绍它，但我绝对认为这是极端的，对吧？

segments.en: And so we have this phrase, draconian measures.
segments.zh: 所以我们有这个短语，严厉的措施。

segments.en: Right, they mentioned that in the dialogue.
segments.zh: 对，他们在对话中提到了这一点。

segments.en: Yeah, so draconian, something that's draconian is excessive or severe, you know?
segments.zh: 是的，所以严厉，严厉的东西是过度的或严重的，你知道吗？

segments.en: And I think that there are a lot of reasons not to have the death penalty, because the death penalty, well, you're pretty much saying we as a society think that murder is wrong, but we're going to show you that you've done a wrong thing, like a bad thing that's against the law by killing you.
segments.zh: 而且我认为有很多理由没有死刑，因为死刑，嗯，你几乎是说我们作为一个社会认为谋杀是错误的，但我们会向你表明你做错了什么，就像一个违法的坏事，因为杀了你而违反了法律。

segments.en: All right, and so I have to disagree with that on a philosophical level.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以我不得不在哲学层面上不同意这一点。

segments.en: But what about practical?
segments.zh: 但是实用呢？

segments.en: Practically speaking, I think that there are a lot of problems with the prison system and the legal system in the United States, for example, because prisons are really crowded.
segments.zh: 实际上，我认为美国的监狱系统和法律制度存在很多问题，例如，因为监狱真的很拥挤。

segments.en: 1% of the American population is in prison.
segments.zh: 1%的美国人口在监狱中。

segments.en: And so I think that so long as the prison system still has problems, there's a really good argument for having the death penalty.
segments.zh: 所以我认为只要监狱系统仍然存在问题，就有一个非常好的论据来判处死刑。

segments.en: But still, I think that it's excessive and it's unnecessary and that there are other ways to treat and punish prisoners.
segments.zh: 但是，我仍然认为这是过度的，这是不必要的，还有其他方法可以对待和惩罚囚犯。

segments.en: It is an interesting topic because you have many different angles that are in favor or against the death penalty.
segments.zh: 这是一个有趣的话题，因为你有许多支持或反对死刑的不同角度。

segments.en: For example, you have religious views where you say that you should not take a life of another person no matter what.
segments.zh: 例如，你有宗教观点，你说无论如何你都不应该夺走另一个人的生命。

segments.en: Or you have other views that say that the death penalty is simply wrong and that you can't right a wrong with another wrong.
segments.zh: 或者你有其他观点说死刑完全是错误的，你不能纠正错误和另一个错误。

segments.en: Right, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: So it kind of doesn't make sense.
segments.zh: 所以这有点没有意义。

segments.en: But at the same time, you do, like you say, the prisons are full of people and it costs around I think it's $12,000 a year per person to keep them in prison.
segments.zh: 但与此同时，就像你说的那样，监狱里到处都是人，而且我认为将他们关在监狱里需要每年 12,000 美元。

segments.en: So what do you do with all of these people that have life sentences that are going to spend the rest of their lives in jail?
segments.zh: 那么，您如何处理所有这些被判无期徒刑的人将在监狱中度过余生呢？

segments.en: So it is interesting and many countries are very, very strict with their legal system in comparison with the United States, right?
segments.zh: 所以这很有趣，许多国家与美国相比，他们的法律制度非常非常严格，对吧？

segments.en: Definitely, but there is a statistic that's pretty stunning that I think among the top 20 developed nations in the world, I think only the United States is the one with the death penalty.
segments.zh: 当然，但有一个统计数据非常惊人，我认为在世界前 20 个发达国家中，我认为只有美国是死刑的国家。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: And actually, the ratio of people compared to the population that are in jail is much higher in the United States than in other countries.
segments.zh: 实际上，在美国，人口与监狱人口的比例远高于其他国家。

segments.en: That's true.
segments.zh: 确实如此。

segments.en: So it is a very questionable topic, but we want to know what you think.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个非常有问题的话题，但我们想知道你的想法。

segments.en: Do you think that the death penalty is a justifiable way to do justice?
segments.zh: 你认为死刑是正义的正义方式吗？

segments.en: Or do you think maybe it's just wrong and we shouldn't have it anymore?
segments.zh: 或者你认为这可能是错误的，我们不应该再拥有它？

segments.en: Yeah, we're hoping that this will get the conversation going on our website.
segments.zh: 是的，我们希望这能让我们的网站上进行对话。

segments.en: If you have any opinions, please let us know about them.
segments.zh: 如果您有任何意见，请告诉我们。

segments.en: EnglishPod.com is the website and of course, you can always email us or send us a PM if you're a little bit shy.
segments.zh: Englishpod.com 是网站，当然，如果您有点害羞，您可以随时给我们发送电子邮件或向我们发送 PM。

segments.en: All right, so we'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们会在那里见到你们。

segments.en: Bye everyone.
segments.zh: 大家再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
